terms.gloss: the front; the face of a building, a camp or a line
evidence: Caes. BC 3.37.1: ante frontem castrōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly the forehead, then the front of anything, as against its back (tergum) and its sides. In front is ā fronte (Cic. Phil. 3.32, Lewis & Short; Traupman 319).

evidence: Plin. NH 11.131: ā priōre parte capitis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase for the front of a classroom: prior pars conclāvis scholāris (p. 319).

phrases.latin: omnis habet geminās, hinc atque hinc, jānua frontīs, ē quibus haec populum spectat, at illa Larem
phrases.english: every door has two fronts, this side and that: one looks out on the people, the other on the household god

sources: Lewis & Short: frons · Lewis & Short: pars · Lewis & Short: prior
